problem: Mapless VLM-based object navigators decide mostly from the current observation, so they repeatedly revisit explored regions or get stuck, and they make false-positive target predictions that lead to approaching the wrong object and stopping prematurely.
motivation: Indoor object navigation is partially observable and depends on temporal context. VLMs hallucinate objects from local textures or confuse similar objects. Explicit maps add construction and maintenance overhead, so a lightweight memory plus verification is attractive.
key_idea: Add a geometry-triggered short-term language memory that corrects repetitive VLM direction choices, plus an independent single-view target verification step before approaching and stopping, on top of RAM-tag-augmented panoramic VLM decisions.
insight: The ablation on HM3D v0.2 with Qwen3-VL-4B shows target verification matters most: removing it drops SR from 56.2 to 45.9 while SPL barely changes (21.8 to 21.0). Memory correction removal costs 3.4 SR, and RAM semantic grounding gives only a modest gain (55.4 SR without it). Most gains therefore come from rejecting false positives rather than better exploration, and gains hold under a common weak backbone (+2.7 SR over InstructNav).
method: RAM semantic grounding: Recognize Anything Model extracts object tags from each of six 79° RGB views (yaw 30/90/150/210/270/330), formed into directional priors that are fed to the VLM together with the panorama and target category.
Initial VLM decision: outputs the direction, a target-visible flag, a rationale and a panoramic scene description.
Episodic memory: FIFO buffer of the last K=10 nodes storing world position and the VLM scene description; there is no map and no information about unexplored areas.

Geometry-triggered retrieval: when the target is not visible, past nodes are projected into the current camera view. If any fall in the selected direction's navigable mask within τθ=40°, the furthest matched node's description is retrieved and given to the VLM with a correction prompt to revise the direction.

Target verification: when the target is flagged visible, the VLM re-checks only the selected single view, giving a binary verdict; the flag is the AND of the two. On failure the direction goes back to memory correction.
Depth-based action sampling: candidate collision-free rays from the depth traversability mask are drawn on the RGB image, and the VLM picks one as polar action (r,θ).

Goal estimation and stopping: arrow endpoints during approach are converted to world-frame goal estimates and averaged, and the agent stops when within 0.8 m of the average (benchmark success radius 1.0 m).

setting.backbone: Gemini-3-Flash (frozen) for main results; Qwen3-VL-4B (frozen) for ablations and the common-backbone comparison; RAM (pretrained, frozen) for tags
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (640x480, 79° HFOV) captured as six views for a panorama, plus pose
setting.action_space: polar actions (distance, relative yaw) chosen among depth-sampled candidate rays, mapped to simulator motion, plus stop; max 40 decision steps
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D v0.1, HM3D v0.2, MP3D ObjectNav)
setting.privileged: none (pose is given; GT target position is used only by the evaluator)

numbers.extra: same backbone used for reimplemented baselines

numbers_note: Backbone-sensitivity, memory-capacity and pose-noise results are only in the supplementary material, which is not included. Ablation numbers (Qwen3-VL-4B, HM3D v0.2) are in the insight field.
results: With Gemini-3-Flash, ReMemNav reaches SR/SPL of 49.8/24.3 on MP3D, 60.0/36.8 on HM3D v0.1 and 67.8/36.6 on HM3D v0.2, beating the best training-free baselines by 8.7/6.9 on MP3D and 18.2/11.1 on HM3D v0.2 (e.g. vs VLFM's 62.6/31.0 on v0.2). On v0.1, SR is 1.7 above the best training-free baseline (InstructNav 58.0), but SR is slightly below SGM (60.2, which needs training) while SPL is the highest. With Qwen3-VL-4B it beats InstructNav, UniGoal and VLMNav, and its latency (5660 ms per decision cycle) is comparable to VLMNav.
limitations: Evaluated only in static simulated indoor environments, with no real-robot validation.
The memory holds only the last 10 nodes, so it is not scalable to long-horizon navigation; correction and verification each add an extra VLM call (~3 s) per triggered step.
Relies on given pose/odometry and a strong proprietary VLM for the top results; the gain with a small backbone is modest (SPL +0.7 over InstructNav).
